pr_body:
We have two different locks in the `Streamer` infrastructure: one is for
the `Streamer` itself and another one for the `budget`. Previously,
there was no contract about which mutex needs to be acquired first which
led to the deadlock detector thinking that there is a potential deadlock
situation. This is now fixed by requiring that the `budget`'s mutex is
acquired first and by releasing the `Streamer`'s mutex in `Enqueue`
early in order to not overlap with the interaction with the `budget`.

I believe that it was a false positive (i.e. the deadlock cannot
actually occur) because without the support of pipelining, `Enqueue`
calls and asynchronous requests evaluation never overlap in time.
Still, it's good to fix the order of mutex acquisitions.

Fixes: #74782.
Fixes: #74785.
Fixes: #74787.
Fixes: #74788.
Fixes: #74789.
Fixes: #74790.
Fixes: #74791.

Release note: None
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/74807)

This deadlock detector seems very good, and apparently we're now running it on a nightly basis, so I imagine that it should be able to catch any mistakes in the order of locking in the future as well. I also couldn't think of any way to enforce the order while at the same time we definitely want to have two different mutexes, so it should be ok for now.

TFTR!

bors r+

review_comments:
This is introducing a new race condition, which is objectively worse - it can only be caught by the race detector now, which is less precise/powerful than the deadlock detector.

After `s.mu.Unlock()` in the main body of the function, there's a brief amount of time where `locked` is still `true`.
If the defer is run at that moment, then this condition here `if !locked` will not fire, and `s.mu.err` below becomes a racy write.

Can't this be handled with a buffered channel for s.mu.err instead?

Indeed, nice catch, thanks! I opened up a fix in #75078.

> Can't this be handled with a buffered channel for s.mu.err instead?

The buffered channel could work, but it doesn't seem to be a natural fit for this since, generally speaking, we want to observe the error from multiple goroutines (`workerCoordinator.mainLoop` and `GetResults`).
